minutes.headline: Committee voted to pay staff during COVID closure, froze hiring, cancelled April trip, and deferred DC and Galapagos trips.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting during the COVID-19 school closure. The business manager reported costs the local budget must absorb for food service and extended day staff and grab-and-go meals. The committee voted to keep paying employees, imposed a hiring freeze, cancelled the April music trip, put off decisions on the DC and Galapagos trips, and approved four policies.

public_comment.topic: Call for public comment on agenda items; Mr. Beardmore and Meredith Weiss had no comment.
Second public comment period: no comments from Mr. Beardmore or Meredith Weiss. A caller's remarks about field trips are unclear in the captions.

votes.motion: Approve regular session minutes of March 11 and executive session minutes of February 26.
votes.outcome: passed 5-0 (roll call yes from all five members)

votes.motion: Pay regular wages for hours worked during the closure period, plus grab-and-go program expenses for low-income students, subject to appropriation.
Authorize the superintendent to implement a staff hiring freeze; positions to be posted need committee approval.
Cancel the April music trip to Philadelphia and New York City.
Wait three more weeks before voting again on the eighth grade Washington DC trip.
Waive second reading of policies 5218 and 5218.01.
Approve the four policies as read on third reading.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to keep paying regular wages for hours worked during the COVID-19 closure, plus grab-and-go meals, subject to appropriation.
The committee voted 5-0 to authorize the superintendent to freeze hiring; any position to be posted needs committee approval.
The business manager said food service and extended day staff costs through April 7 must be absorbed by the local budget because the revolving accounts stopped taking in money.
The committee voted 5-0 to cancel the April music trip and 5-0 to wait three more weeks before voting again on the eighth grade Washington DC trip.
The committee waived second reading and approved four policies on third reading, 5-0 each; it made no motion on the Galapagos trip.

why_it_matters: Wages for staff who cannot work and meals for low-income students now draw on the local budget, mostly taxes, because revolving accounts stopped taking in money and federal reimbursement is unclear.
Eighth grade families face a possible lost deposit on the DC trip if it is cancelled, and are being told to hold the final payment while the decision waits.
watch_next: The eighth grade DC trip returns to the committee in about three weeks.
The committee may lift the hiring freeze at a later meeting, and the advisor is to return with an update on the Galapagos trip.
